name: particles implode, spell a word, then converge into a sphere
looks: A point of light on a black field implodes into a burst of fine specks. The specks regather into a word made entirely of dust-sized particles, with a small caption stating the particle count and the kind of flow field driving them, then the same particles stream off and converge into a dense, slowly turning sphere of points.
build: One particle system driven by the master clock: an initial radial burst/implosion seeds each particle's starting position; particles then ease toward sample points of the word's filled glyph shapes (power3.out, seeded per-particle delay) to spell it out, hold briefly, then re-target onto a Fibonacci-sphere distribution for the final convergence, with short light trails on the fastest-moving particles.
sound: A soft implosion whoosh, a granular shimmer as the word resolves, and a rising tone into the sphere's hum.
prompt: Implode a point of light into a cloud of fine particles, let them regather into a single word built entirely out of dust, caption the particle count and the kind of field moving them, then stream the same particles off into a dense, slowly turning sphere, so one particle system carries three different payoffs.
